question.text: A trader buys a USDINR put option with strike 83.50 at Rs. 0.20 premium. At expiry, USDINR is 82.80. Net profit per unit?

explanation.text: The Logic: A long-put exercise payoff is strike minus spot when spot is below strike. Here payoff = 83.50 - 82.80 = Rs. 0.70. Net profit per unit deducts the premium paid: 0.70 - 0.20 = Rs. 0.50. The currency option lot size is 1000 units. The Trap: Rs. 0.70 is the gross payoff before deducting the premium paid by the buyer; net profit must always subtract the premium. Note: Workbook reference — pp.83-85 (long-put payoff, net profit framework, and currency option lot size of 1000 units).
